title: Orchid Edge cutover: terraform notes & sizing cheatsheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures the current working plan for the ‘Orchid’ manufacturing partner private deployment cutover. Focus: Terraform module adjustments, target sizing figures (density + KV cache expectations), and a minimal incremental rollback strategy. This is an engineering working doc — informal, iterative.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Customer: Orchid Manufacturing (on-prem Kubernetes + isolated VPC routing between plant clusters).
- Goal: Migrate Orchid from hosted evaluation to Private deployment (VPC mode) with a 4-week phased cutover, maintaining 99.5% P95 latency SLO for inference and <2% model-quality regressions.
- Primary constraints: single-rack GPU clusters per site (NVIDIA L40x2 equivalent), limited cross-site bandwidth (10–50 Mbps interconnect), strict air-gapped windows during final cutover.

Key assumptions (callouts):
- Orchids' production traffic profile: 120 QPS average inference requests across 3 edge sites during peak; median seq len 512, tail to 2048 for batched analytics jobs run nights.
- KV cache hit target: 65% for steady-state (we size for 70% headroom).
- Quantization: customer agreed to int8 quantized variants for non-critical pipelines; critical models run fp16.
- Monitoring: customer has Prometheus + Grafana; we will deploy our agent with 30-day retention for traces.
- Maintenance windows: weekly nightly window 02:00–04:00 local; final cutover requires a 6-hour scheduled blackout.

Sizing matrix (per site):
- GPUs: 4 x L40-equivalent (single-rack), reserved for inference pool.
- CPU: 32 vCPU per node (k8s nodes sized as 8 nodes each with 4 vCPU), control-plane nodes separate (3x m4-class).
- Memory: 512Gi total per GPU node (to support multiple model variants + quant caches).
- Disk: 2TB NVMe per node, with 500Gi for model cache.
- Network: 10Gb internal fabric; inter-site uplink limited to 50Mbps (plan accordingly for cross-site replication).

Why these numbers: workload modeling based on Redwood runtime perf profiles for seq=512 and 1024; measured throughput at p95 with int8 quant shows ~2.8x token/sec improvement vs fp16. We prioritized GPU count to hit 120 QPS with autoscaling headroom but limited rack space.

Terraform module notes (high-priority changes):
- module path: modules/edge-cluster-vpc
  - New var: allowlist_subnets (list of cidr) — required to chat with Orchids' control plane. Default null.
  - New output: node_pool_autoscaler_state (string) — set to disabled/enabled explicitly to prevent surprise autoscale during cutover.
- module path: modules/storage-model-cache
  - Change: expose lifecycle ignore_changes = ["aws_ebs_volume[model_cache].size"] for onprem infra shim to permit manual expansion during cutover without TF diffs.
- module path: modules/networking/vpc-peering
  - Add validation for max_bandwidth_mbps var — warn if >100 to avoid accidental config that exceeds on-prem circuit.

Terraform workflow hints:
- Use workspace per site: tf workspace new orchid-site-a; keeps state separate and reduces blast radius.
- Locking: enable remote state with state-lock (consul/backends). For on-prem customers we will use S3-style object store provided by customer behind a presigned gateway — document access credentials and rotation.

Upgrade and cutover plan (phased):
1) Preflight (week 0–1): collect final inventories (NIC speeds, OOB access, KMS endpoint), confirm signed cutover window. Run infra-lint (internal) to identify module diffs.
2) Staging deployment (week 1): deploy same TF plan to customer staging cluster; sanity tests: model load, KV cache priming scripts, concurrent QPS soak (2x expected).
3) Canary (week 2): small % of traffic routed to private cluster (10%). Monitor latency, token cost, and model output drift. If drift >2% on eval suite, rollback to hosted routing.
4) Bulk cutover (week 3): escalate to 50% -> 100% over 6h blackout, with ops on call.
5) Post-cutover stabilization (week 3–4): tighten SLIs and run traffic replays to verify tails.

Cutover checklist (short):
- [ ] Confirm TF workspace per site created and locked.
- [ ] Customer KMS provisioning complete; test encrypt/decrypt cycle with sample key.
- [ ] Model bundle mirroring validated (sha256 checksums match).
- [ ] Prometheus scrape targets added; alerting thresholds published to customer.
- [ ] Autoscaler explicitly disabled during DB migrations/cutover step.
- [ ] Backup of hosted routing table and DNS TTL lowered to 60s.

Rollback strategy (minimal):
- Immediate rollback: flip routing back to hosted API (low-latency path) and scale down edge pool. Requires DNS reversion and rollback of any model commits made in private environment.
- Partial rollback: revert to canary % (10%) if metrics show regression but not full failure.
- Terraform-level rollback: apply previous tfstate snapshot (workspaces make this quick) — manual verification required for storage size drifts.

Model + runtime operational notes:
- KV cache sizing calculation: assume average context 1024 tokens, avg payload 2.2KB; with 70% hit target, reserve ~180GB cache per site. Use LRU with 10% prefetch slack.
- Batch sizing suggestions: default continuous batching 64ms aggregation window; for Orchid latency-critical pipelines reduce to 12ms for p95 improvements. Test with loadgen.
- Kernel selection: prefer fused attention kernels for seq <= 1024; set runtime hint in config: redwood.runtime.kernel_hint = "fused_attention" for critical pods.

Open questions (needs customer confirmation):
- Can Orchid accept presigned-state gateways for TF remote state? If not, we need to set up a Consul server (extra OOB setup).
- Are there any on-prem filesystem quotas that would interrupt model cache growth beyond 1TB?
- Confirm security contact and out-of-band escalation phone for blackout.

TODOs (short-term):
- Ravi: produce tf plan diff and share pr to private-deploy repo (GH PR link in linked_artifacts). Due EOD Thu.
- Maya: run KV cache sizing script with Orchid sample traces and paste results into this doc.
- Diego: draft Ops runbook for rollback steps and get customer sign-off on escalation policy.

Notes-from-last-sanity-run:
- We saw a 12% increase in p95 when autoscaler kicks during model reload; disable autoscaling during model-promotion windows.
- Model checksum mismatch once in staging — add sha256 verification to model-deploy helm hooks.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- tf workspaces: terraform workspace select orchid-site-a || terraform workspace new orchid-site-a
- plan for specific module: terraform plan -target=module.edge-cluster-vpc -out=orchid-edge.plan
- apply with approval: terraform apply "orchid-edge.plan"
- KV cache priming: scripts/prime-kv.sh --bundle s3://orchid/models/v1 --concurrency 8

End of doc — this is a living draft. Drop comments inline or ping #private-deploy in Slack for urgent notes.
